ms.promise:
- Open source code that takes raw blockchain data (assumed to be pre-validated) and a wallet’s credentials and returns a list of all transactions related to that wallet, including the information on whether each transaction is spent or not (a UTxO).
- Benchmarks of the code proving that it can reconstruct a wallet’s transaction history in one hour or less on modern hardware (8+-core CPU, sufficient RAM, fast SSD).
- An estimate of the algorithm’s data-processing throughput, allowing to set requirements for the networking-scalability analysis in milestone 2.

For this milestone, the code will focus on a simple but widespread use case:
- A wallet that uses only Shelley-era addresses with a stake key (type 0 address).
- ADA transactions only.
- Staking rewards not considered.

For this milestone, the project team offers payment-on-delivery terms subject to the IOG’s agreement to review the deliverables within four weeks of the milestone completion.

The estimated duration of this milestone is four months: three months for the development and one month for the review by IOG.
ms.criteria:
- The delivered code can achieve the promised improvement - reconstruct a wallet’s transaction history (matching the requirements set in the Outputs section) in one hour or less.
- If the payment-on-delivery offer is accepted, the IOG shall provide a statement of acceptance/concern within four weeks of the milestone completion. If no statement is made within four weeks from the milestone completion, the milestone is to be considered as completed automatically.
ms.report:
The deliverables for milestone 1 are:
1) Open-source code of the highly-parallel wallet-history reconstruction method: https://github.com/sierkov/daedalus-turbo
2) A research report explaining the method, presenting its benchmarks, and evaluating its data-processing throughput: https://github.com/sierkov/daedalus-turbo/blob/main/doc/2023_Sierkov_WalletHistoryReconstruction.pdf
3) An estimate of the method's data-processing throughput to be used as the reference for the research in milestone 2: 4000 MB/sec (four thousand megabytes per second). For details, please see the research report.

The acceptance criterium for this milestone is that the code can reconstruct a wallet's history from raw blockchain data in one hour or quicker. On a modern computer (8+ core CPU, fast SSD), the submitted code can reconstruct a wallet's history in one minute.

ms.report:
This is the fourth submission of M2 PoA prepared in response to the review submitted on May 27, 2024, reviewing the third M2 PoA submission made on November 20, 2023. It starts with an introductory comment and then provides the updated materials.
First, it’s important to note that on April 30, 2024, a submission of PoA materials for the third milestone (M3) of the project was made: https://milestones.projectcatalyst.io/projects/900076/milestones/3. It provides additional details on the security approach, a POC implementation of the method, and a discussion of the project's immediate plans. From the review submitted on May 27, 2024, it’s unclear if those materials had been available to the reviewer, so in the below comment those materials are referenced again where they address the discussed issues.
Second, the characterization of the project’s approach as a “light wallet” is incorrect. The fundamental differences with light wallets are that the validation of the blockchain data is performed completely on client devices and that client devices have a full copy of the blockchain data allowing the wallet software to adaptively decide on the most appropriate validation approach given the use case and the current user need. For the above reasons, a characterization as an adaptive full wallet is believed to be more appropriate. The word adaptive highlights that the capability of a wallet to dynamically adjust the validation procedure tailoring it to the current needs of the wallet’s owner. The following document describes the current vision for the security model and explains why this approach is believed to have at least equivalent security to that of normal Daedalus: https://github.com/sierkov/daedalus-turbo/blob/main/doc/2024-sierkov-on-wallet-security.pdf

ms.report:
Introduction
This submission presents the full proof-of-concept of the new synchronization and wallet-history-reconstruction algorithms fitted into a user-testable application: a local blockchain explorer that works without wallet private keys for additional user safety.
The presented deliverables not only meet but noticeably exceed the targets set by the proposal, showcasing the project's capability to deliver beyond expectations:
・Performance: A modern 8-core laptop, a MacBook Air M2, with 250 Mbps Internet connection, can synchronize the chain from scratch in about 35 minutes, which noticeably better than the target of one hour.
・Security: The proposed security approach offers better security properties than Mithril and is comparable to the standard Daedalus configuration using Cardano Node and Cardano Wallet.

At the same time, the project had to deliver this milestone in the face of significant headwinds: the milestone funding has not been released, making it impossible to perform the planned broad community testing and verify the compatibility of developed software components with a wide range of hardware and software configurations. Nevertheless, the project team is confident that the presented deliverables fully satisfy the original intent of the proposal.
It's crucial to note that this milestone is not about delivering the final product but about proving beyond reasonable doubt that the presented components allow building a final product while relying on everyday software development practices without additional breakthrough innovation.
The specific evidence is provided below.

The open source code has been published into the project's GitHub repository: https://github.com/sierkov/daedalus-turbo

ms.promise:
The Turbo mode, a combination of an optimized-network-delivery mechanism for blockchain data and a fast transaction-history-reconstruction algorithm, is available as a setting in official builds of Daedalus and allows for a clean Daedalus installation with a newly created wallet to be synced and ready for use in one hour or less, assuming modern hardware and a sufficient Internet connection.Daedalus in the Turbo mode can:
- sync blockchain data and reconstruct a typical wallet's transaction history from scratch in one hour or less on modern hardware (8+-core CPU, sufficient RAM, fast SSD) and with a sufficient Internet connection (at least 250 MBits/sec).
- sync one month of recent blockchain data and reconstruct a typical wallet's transaction history for that period in five minutes or less on modern hardware (8+-core CPU, sufficient RAM, fast SSD) and with sufficient Internet connection (at least 250 MBits/sec).
